title: Patch 19 - Arithmetic Reasoning Content & AFOQT Practice Test
description: Align Arithmetic Reasoning content with topic/difficulty structure, index question JSON files, and stand up an AFOQT-style Arithmetic Reasoning practice test.

notesForCopilot: Each JSON file represents a batch of questions for a single Arithmetic Reasoning subtopic and difficulty level.
Use the filename to infer subtopicId and difficulty (e.g., `ratio_proportion_word_problems_beginner_part1.json` → subtopicId = `ratio_proportion_word_problems`, difficulty = `beginner`).
Aggregate all parts for the same (subtopicId, difficulty) pair into a single in-memory question pool when the app loads.

mappedGameSubtopics.description: Straightforward story problems using basic operations and rate = work/time setups.
Word problems where the core step is building and solving a proportion or interpreting ratios.
Percent-of, discount/markup, and basic interest-like problems framed verbally.
Mixing, comparing, and operating with fractions/decimals in context (fuel usage, distances, etc.).
Multiple workers, pipelines, and travel problems where time, rate, and work interact.
Simple probability with dice, cards, selections, and basic independent events.
Translating word problems into linear equations and solving for unknown quantities.
Mean and weighted mean in context, including finding missing value given average and count.

logicForCopilot: When loading Arithmetic Reasoning questions, iterate over all JSON files in the Arithmetic content directory.
Parse each filename according to the pattern `<subtopicId>_<difficulty>_part<index>.json`.
Insert questions into an in-memory registry keyed as: `questions['arithmetic_reasoning'][subtopicId][difficulty]`.

For example, `time_rate_work_word_problems_beginner_part1.json` and `time_rate_work_word_problems_beginner_part2.json` both append to `questions['arithmetic_reasoning']['time_rate_work_word_problems']['beginner']`.
Use `subjects[].mappedGameSubtopics` to confirm that a given subtopicId is known and to drive UI labels.

studyMode.description: Immediate feedback after each question for learning.

practiceTestMode.description: Simulated AFOQT environment; no feedback until test completion.

globalInstructionForCopilot: Update Arithmetic Reasoning to support both `studyMode` and `practiceTestMode` aligned with other AFOQT subjects.
In `studyMode`, show correctness and explanation immediately after each question.
In `practiceTestMode`, hide correctness and explanations until the entire Arithmetic section is complete, then show a summary report.
Ensure the UI clearly indicates which mode is active before the user begins answering questions.

globalRules: For each main AFOQT subject flagged with `isAfoqtOfficialSubject = true`, including Arithmetic Reasoning, create a dedicated practice test entry titled `AFOQT <DisplayName> Practice Test`.
Each AFOQT practice test must only pull questions from subtopics where `isOfficialAfoqtTopic = true`.
Each AFOQT practice test automatically runs in `practiceTestMode` by default to simulate real test conditions.
Within a subject, question selection should sample across all difficulty levels with a bias toward `advanced` and `beginner`, with a smaller share from `expert`.

selectionLogicForCopilot: Merge all questions for the included Arithmetic subtopics and difficulty tiers into a temporary pool.
Randomly sample questions according to the configured difficultyDistribution.
Avoid duplicate questions within a single test run.
If a requested quota for a given difficulty cannot be met (pool too small), backfill from the nearest difficulty level (e.g., advanced → beginner or expert) while maintaining total test length.

implementationNotesForCopilot: 1. Index all Arithmetic Reasoning JSON files at startup using the naming convention described in `arithmeticContent.fileNamingConvention`.
3. Wire the Arithmetic Reasoning practice test entry into the game's test selection UI alongside other AFOQT practice tests.
4. Ensure that mode behavior (study vs practiceTestMode) is consistent with what Patch 18 introduced for vocabulary-style subjects.
5. Keep implementation generic so that adding new Arithmetic JSON content (new parts, new difficulties) automatically expands the pool without requiring code changes.
6. Do not expose internal file paths to the end user; only use `displayName` and high-level labels in the UI.
